# OpenLineageSqlExt in datafusion_openlineage::session - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/session/trait.OpenLineageSqlExt.html

`pub trait OpenLineageSqlExt: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required methods
    fn [with_lineage](https://docs.rs#tymethod.with_lineage)(
        self,
        builder: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[OpenLineageBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html)>>,
    ) -> Self;
[try_with_lineage_from_env](https://docs.rs#tymethod.try_with_lineage_from_env)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ClientError](https://docs.rs/enum.ClientError.html)>;
[sql_with_lineage](https://docs.rs#tymethod.sql_with_lineage)<'life0, 'life1, 'async_trait>(
        &'life0 self,
        sql: &'life1 [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    ) -> [Pin](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/pin/struct.Pin.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [DataFusionResult](https://docs.rs/datafusion-common/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion_common/error/type.Result.html)<[DataFrame](https://docs.rs/datafusion/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion/dataframe/struct.DataFrame.html)>> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'async_trait>>
       where Self: 'async_trait,
             'life0: 'async_trait,
             'life1: 'async_trait;
}## Expand description

`SessionContext` ergonomics for OpenLineage instrumentation.

Two conveniences over [ OpenLineageBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html):

- `with_lineage`- `SessionContext::enable_url_table(self) -> Self`. It saves the host the- `SessionContext::new_with_state(builder.instrument(ctx.state()))`dance. It takes- `impl Into<Option<OpenLineageBuilder>>`, so- `ctx.with_lineage(None)`uses defaults (a no-op client, default config) and- `ctx.with_lineage(OpenLineage::builder()…)`supplies a configured one.
- `sql_with_lineage`- *with*lineage for statements DataFusion executes outside the query-planner hook —- `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT`and- `CREATE VIEW … AS SELECT`.- `SessionContext::sql`dispatches these DDL statements straight to the catalog before the instrumented- `QueryPlanner`ever sees the full plan, so the created dataset is silently dropped from lineage (and a- `CREATE VIEW`emits nothing at all). For every other statement this is exactly- `SessionContext::sql(...).await`and the normal planner path produces the lineage.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/datafusion_openlineage/session.rs.html#226)#### fn [with_lineage](https://docs.rs#tymethod.with_lineage)(self, builder: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[OpenLineageBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html)>>) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/datafusion_openlineage/session.rs.html#226)

#### fn [with_lineage](https://docs.rs#tymethod.with_lineage)(self, builder: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[OpenLineageBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html)>>) -> Self

Instrument this context with OpenLineage and return it (consume-and-return,
like `SessionContext::enable_url_table`).

Pass a configured [ OpenLineageBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html) to control the transport/client,
context provider, and config — or

`None` for defaults (a no-op client and
[). Because the argument is](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html#method.for_datafusion)

`OpenLineageConfig::for_datafusion``impl Into<Option<OpenLineageBuilder>>`, both `ctx.with_lineage(None)` and
`ctx.with_lineage(OpenLineage::builder()…)` are valid call sites. For the
standard-environment path use [(it is fallible, so it can’t fold into this signature).](https://docs.rs/trait.OpenLineageSqlExt.html#tymethod.try_with_lineage_from_env)

`try_with_lineage_from_env`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/datafusion_openlineage/session.rs.html#234)#### fn [try_with_lineage_from_env](https://docs.rs#tymethod.try_with_lineage_from_env)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ClientError](https://docs.rs/enum.ClientError.html)>

# datafusion_openlineage::client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/client/index.html

## Expand description

The OpenLineage client: a non-blocking emit front-end over a [ Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html).

Emission must never break or slow the host query. [ OpenLineageClient::emit](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.emit)
is non-blocking: it hands the event to a bounded channel drained by a
background task that delivers events to the transport (coalescing queued
events into batches when the upstream is slow) and swallows + logs any error.
If the channel is full the event is dropped with a warning (back-pressure must
not stall planning).

[drains the queue and flushes the transport before exit.](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.shutdown)

`OpenLineageClient::shutdown`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html)- Lineage - Client
- Non-blocking front-end for emitting OpenLineage events.
- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClientBuilder.html)- Lineage - Client - Builder
- Builder for `OpenLineageClient`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Client](https://docs.rs/enum.ClientError.html)- Error
- Error returned when an `OpenLineageClient`

---

# datafusion_openlineage::cloud - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/cloud/index.html

## Expand description

Default HTTP transport backed by [ olai_http::CloudClient](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html).

`CloudClient` handles auth (bearer token, Databricks, AWS/GCP credentials,
or unauthenticated) and retry/backoff, so this transport works against
deployed, authenticated OpenLineage endpoints out of the box. It does not add
its own retry loop; it does bound each request with a timeout so one hung
upstream request cannot stall the shared background drain.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cloud](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudClientTransport.html)- Client - Transport
- Posts OpenLineage events to an HTTP endpoint via `CloudClient`

---

#### pub async fn [sign_and_send](https://docs.rs#method.sign_and_send)(&self, request: [Request](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/reqwest/async_impl/request/struct.Request.html)) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[Response](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/reqwest/async_impl/response/struct.Response.html)>

Sign an already-built [ reqwest::Request](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/reqwest/async_impl/request/struct.Request.html) and dispatch it, with retries.

This is the request-level counterpart to the [ CloudRequestBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudRequestBuilder.html)
flow: it applies the client’s

[(refreshing credentials as needed) and sends the request through the configured](https://docs.rs/trait.RequestSigner.html)

`RequestSigner`[, retrying transient failures per the client’s](https://docs.rs/service/trait.HttpService.html)

`HttpService`[. It is useful when the request is produced elsewhere (for example by a protocol stack such as ConnectRPC) and only needs authentication and transport.](https://docs.rs/struct.RetryConfig.html)

`RetryConfig`The request body must be in memory (not a stream): retries clone the request, and provider signers such as AWS SigV4 hash the body to sign it.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an [ Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) if signing fails or if the request ultimately fails
after exhausting retries. A non-success HTTP status code is not itself an
error; inspect

[on the returned response.](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.28/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/reqwest/async_impl/response/struct.Response.html#method.status)

# datafusion_openlineage::column - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/column/index.html

## Expand description

Sound column-level lineage extraction from a DataFusion [ LogicalPlan](https://docs.rs/datafusion-expr/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion_expr/logical_plan/plan/enum.LogicalPlan.html).

Walks the *optimized* plan bottom-up, maintaining for every node a map of
*output schema position -> set of physical  (dataset, column) sources*.
Indexing by position (never by name) is what makes the resolution
scope-sound: column refs in expressions resolve to child positions via

`DFSchema::maybe_index_of_column`, so qualifiers participate exactly as
DataFusion’s own scoping does and aliases/CTEs/self-joins can neither
collide nor fabricate datasets. Only the root node’s map is published, and
the facet is attached to the **output**datasets, keyed by output field (see

`docs/open-lineage-design.md`).Degradation policy: any unhandled node, arity mismatch, unresolvable column
ref, or expression embedding a subquery drops column lineage for the whole
statement (`None`). A partially-correct per-column facet is
indistinguishable from a complete one to consumers, so whole-facet drop is
the only honest partial failure. There is deliberately no name-based
fallback. Table-level lineage is unaffected.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Column](https://docs.rs/struct.ColumnSources.html)- Sources
- The direct sources of one output column.
- [Resolved](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolvedColumns.html)- Columns
- Column lineage for the dataset a root `Dml`/`Ddl`plan writes: output field name -> sources, plus the statement-wide indirect influences.
- [Source](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceColumn.html)- Column
- A physical source column in a real input dataset.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Direct](https://docs.rs/enum.DirectKind.html)- Kind
- How directly a source value feeds an output column. Ordered so that merging two paths to the same source keeps the strongest claim.
- [Indirect](https://docs.rs/enum.IndirectKind.html)- Kind
- How a source influences output rows without its value flowing into them.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Indirect](https://docs.rs/type.IndirectSources.html)- Sources
- Per-source indirect influences; unions upward through the plan.

---

# datafusion_openlineage::config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/config/index.html

## Expand description

DataFusion engine identity for [ OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html).

[ OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html) itself is engine-agnostic and lives in

[. This module adds](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/index.html)

`openlineage_client`[, an extension trait that stamps the DataFusion](https://docs.rs/trait.DataFusionConfig.html)

`DataFusionConfig``processing_engine` identity (name +
[) and a DataFusion-flavored producer.](https://docs.rs/datafusion/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion/constant.DATAFUSION_VERSION.html)

`datafusion::DATAFUSION_VERSION`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)- Lineage - Config
- Identifies the emitting integration on every emitted event/facet, and tunes the emit transport.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DATAFUSION_](https://docs.rs/constant.DATAFUSION_PRODUCER.html)- PRODUCER
- The `producer`URI stamped on events emitted by this integration.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/config.rs.html#57)

#### pub fn [from_env](https://docs.rs#method.from_env)() -> [OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)

Build a config from the standard OpenLineage environment conventions.

Reads `OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` for the default job namespace (falling back
to [ DEFAULT_NAMESPACE](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/config/constant.DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.html)) and

`OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` for the request
timeout (falling back to [); the producer/adapter identity is fixed for this crate and the engine identity is left empty (an engine integration such as](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/config/constant.DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.html)

`DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT``datafusion-openlineage` stamps it). This is
the documented entry point for env-driven configuration — pair it with
[, which reads](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.from_env)

`OpenLineageClient::from_env``OPENLINEAGE_URL` / `OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT` / `OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY`
for the transport, so an integration can wire itself up entirely from the
environment the rest of the OpenLineage ecosystem already uses.[ Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) is equivalent and reads the same environment;

`from_env`
exists to make the env dependency explicit and discoverable at call sites.[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/config.rs.html#69)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/config.rs.html#69)

[ Self::from_env](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html#method.from_env) with the

`OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` / `OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS`
values injected, so the fallback logic is unit-testable without mutating
process-global env. An absent or empty namespace falls back to
[; an absent/empty/unparsable timeout falls back to](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/config/constant.DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.html)

`DEFAULT_NAMESPACE`[.](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/config/constant.DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.html)

## Expand description

The DataFusion-specific context-provider seam.

The context *data* ([ LineageContext](https://docs.rs/struct.LineageContext.html)) and its environment conventions live
in

[; this module adds the DataFusion-flavored](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/index.html)

`openlineage_client`[trait, whose](https://docs.rs/trait.LineageContextProvider.html)

`LineageContextProvider`[method receives the query’s](https://docs.rs/trait.LineageContextProvider.html#tymethod.context)

`context`[. A different engine would define its own provider over its own request type.](https://docs.rs/datafusion/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion/execution/session_state/struct.SessionState.html)

`SessionState`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

# datafusion_openlineage::exec - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/exec/index.html

## Expand description

Physical-plan wrapper that emits COMPLETE / FAIL at end of execution.

[ crate::rule::OpenLineageQueryPlanner](https://docs.rs/rule/struct.OpenLineageQueryPlanner.html) emits START at plan time and carries
a COMPLETE template through the plan in a

[;](https://docs.rs/rule/struct.LineageMarker.html)

`crate::rule::LineageMarker`[lowers that marker into an](https://docs.rs/rule/struct.LineageExtensionPlanner.html)

`crate::rule::LineageExtensionPlanner`[at the physical root. This node observes the result streams and emits exactly one terminal event once every output partition has finished:](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageExec.html)

`OpenLineageExec`- COMPLETE when all partitions drain successfully;
- FAIL (with an `errorMessage`run facet) if any partition yields an error or is dropped before its stream is exhausted (e.g. a cancelled query).

Completion is tracked with a `Drop`-based guard so cancellation is handled
without special-casing, and the terminal event fires under the *same*
`runId` the START used.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageExec.html)- Lineage - Exec
- Wraps the root physical plan, emitting a terminal lineage event when execution finishes.

---

# datafusion_openlineage::extract - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/extract/index.html

## Expand description

Extract table-level lineage (input/output datasets + schema) from a
DataFusion [ LogicalPlan](https://docs.rs/datafusion-expr/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion_expr/logical_plan/plan/enum.LogicalPlan.html).

Follows the same `TreeNodeVisitor`-over-`LogicalPlan` shape the Cedar policy
integration uses. Run this on the *optimized* plan so projections/filters are
pushed down to the scans.

Column-level lineage is resolved separately by [ crate::column](https://docs.rs/column/index.html) (a
positional bottom-up walk) and attached to the output datasets here.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputTable.html)- Table
- A dataset a query reads, with its schema.
- [Output](https://docs.rs/struct.OutputTable.html)- Table
- A dataset a query writes, with its schema and optional column lineage.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/struct.QueryLineage.html)- Lineage
- What a query reads and writes.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [extract](https://docs.rs/fn.extract.html)
- Extract `QueryLineage`

---

# datafusion_openlineage::facets - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/facets/index.html

## Expand description

OpenLineage facet types.

Every facet embeds a [ BaseFacet](https://docs.rs/struct.BaseFacet.html) carrying the spec-mandated

`_producer` and
`_schemaURL` fields (underscore-prefixed to avoid collisions with the facet
payload). Shapes follow the OpenLineage spec; see
[https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/facets/](https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/facets/).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Base](https://docs.rs/struct.BaseFacet.html)- Facet
- Common fields present on every OpenLineage facet.
- [Column](https://docs.rs/struct.ColumnLineageDatasetFacet.html)- Lineage - Dataset - Facet
- How an output dataset’s fields derive from input dataset fields.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.DataSourceDatasetFacet.html)- Source - Dataset - Facet
- The physical data source backing a dataset (the `dataSource`dataset facet).
- [Dataset](https://docs.rs/struct.DatasetFacets.html)- Facets
- Bag of dataset facets. Known facets are typed; anything else flows through
`extra`.
- [Documentation](https://docs.rs/struct.DocumentationJobFacet.html)- JobFacet
- Free-text description of a job (the `documentation`job facet).
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorMessageRunFacet.html)- Message - RunFacet
- Failure details attached to a failed run (the `errorMessage`run facet).
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldLineage.html)- Lineage
- Provenance of a single output column.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputDatasetFacets.html)- Dataset - Facets
- Input-only dataset facets (serialized under `inputFacets`).
- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputField.html)- Field
- A source `(dataset, field)`an output column derives from, with how.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputStatisticsInputDatasetFacet.html)- Statistics - Input - Dataset - Facet
- Runtime statistics about the data read from an input dataset.
- [JobFacets](https://docs.rs/struct.JobFacets.html)
- Bag of job facets. Known facets are typed; anything else flows through
`extra`.
- [JobType](https://docs.rs/struct.JobTypeJobFacet.html)- JobFacet
- Classifies a job by processing mode, integration, and type (the `jobType`job facet).
- [Lifecycle](https://docs.rs/struct.LifecycleStateChangeDatasetFacet.html)- State - Change - Dataset - Facet
- The lifecycle state change a run applied to a dataset (the
`lifecycleStateChange`dataset facet).
- [Nominal](https://docs.rs/struct.NominalTimeRunFacet.html)- Time - RunFacet
- The nominal (scheduled) start and end times of a run.
- [Output](https://docs.rs/struct.OutputDatasetFacets.html)- Dataset - Facets
- Output-only dataset facets (serialized under `outputFacets`).
- [Output](https://docs.rs/struct.OutputStatisticsOutputDatasetFacet.html)- Statistics - Output - Dataset - Facet
- Runtime statistics about the data written to an output dataset.
- [Owner](https://docs.rs/struct.Owner.html)
- One owner entry of an `OwnershipJobFacet``MAINTAINER`, or a custom value like`team`/`user`).
- [Ownership](https://docs.rs/struct.OwnershipJobFacet.html)- JobFacet
- Who owns a job (the `ownership`job facet).
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.ParentJob.html)- Job
- Reference to a parent job by namespace and name.
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.ParentRun.html)- Run
- Reference to a parent run by its run identifier.
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.ParentRunFacet.html)- RunFacet
- Links this run to a parent (and optionally root) run/job — set by orchestrators.
- [Processing](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessingEngineRunFacet.html)- Engine - RunFacet
- The facet a query engine is expected to populate to identify itself.
- [Root](https://docs.rs/struct.RootParent.html)- Parent
- The root run and job at the top of a multi-level parent chain.
- [RunFacets](https://docs.rs/struct.RunFacets.html)
- Bag of run facets. Known facets are typed; anything supplied by a
`crate::context::LineageContext``extra`.
- [Schema](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemaDatasetFacet.html)- Dataset - Facet
- The field-level schema of a dataset (the `schema`dataset facet).
- [Schema](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemaField.html)- Field
- One field of a `SchemaDatasetFacet`
- [SqlJob](https://docs.rs/struct.SqlJobFacet.html)- Facet
- The SQL query executed by a job (the `sql`job facet).
- [Symlink](https://docs.rs/struct.SymlinkIdentifier.html)- Identifier
- One alternate identifier of a `SymlinksDatasetFacet`
- [Symlinks](https://docs.rs/struct.SymlinksDatasetFacet.html)- Dataset - Facet
- Alternate identifiers for a dataset (the `symlinks`dataset facet).
- [Tags](https://docs.rs/struct.TagsJobFacet.html)- JobFacet
- Business tags on a job (the `tags`job facet).
- [Tags](https://docs.rs/struct.TagsJobFacetFields.html)- JobFacet - Fields
- One tag of a `TagsJobFacet`
- [Transformation](https://docs.rs/struct.Transformation.html)
- How an input influences an output: `DIRECT`(the source value flows into the output) or`INDIRECT`(influence via filter/group/join/sort).`subtype`is conventionally one of`IDENTITY`,`TRANSFORMATION`,`AGGREGATION`,`FILTER`,`JOIN`,`GROUP_BY`,`SORT`,`WINDOW`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Transformation](https://docs.rs/enum.TransformationType.html)- Type
- Kind of influence an input field has on an output field.

# datafusion_openlineage::naming - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/naming/index.html

## Expand description

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

# datafusion_openlineage::session - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/session/index.html

## Expand description

The customer-facing entry point: [ OpenLineage::builder](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineage.html#method.builder).

One builder assembles the three pieces an integration needs — a
[ Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html)/

[, a](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html)

`OpenLineageClient`[, and an](https://docs.rs/context/trait.LineageContextProvider.html)

`LineageContextProvider`[— and installs them on a](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)

`OpenLineageConfig``SessionState`. The common
case is [followed by](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html#method.from_env)

`OpenLineageBuilder::from_env`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html#method.instrument)

`OpenLineageBuilder::instrument`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineage.html)- Lineage
- Entry point for instrumenting a DataFusion session with OpenLineage.
- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageBuilder.html)- Lineage - Builder
- Builds and installs OpenLineage instrumentation on a `SessionState`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/trait.OpenLineageSqlExt.html)- Lineage - SqlExt
- `SessionContext`ergonomics for OpenLineage instrumentation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [instrument_](https://docs.rs/fn.instrument_session_state.html)- session_ - state
- Instrument `state`with an explicit client, context provider, and config.
- [instrument_](https://docs.rs/fn.instrument_session_state_simple.html)- session_ - state_ - simple
- Instrument `state`with an empty`StaticContextProvider`

---

# datafusion_openlineage::transport - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/transport/index.html

## Expand description

Pluggable sink for OpenLineage events.

Mirrors OpenLineage’s own `Transport` SPI naming. The default
[ NoopTransport](https://docs.rs/struct.NoopTransport.html) is used when no endpoint is configured;

[is handy for development and tests.](https://docs.rs/struct.ConsoleTransport.html)

`ConsoleTransport`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Console](https://docs.rs/struct.ConsoleTransport.html)- Transport
- Logs each event as pretty JSON via `tracing`. For development/tests.
- [Noop](https://docs.rs/struct.NoopTransport.html)- Transport
- Drops events. The safe default when lineage is not configured.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Transport](https://docs.rs/enum.TransportError.html)- Error
- Error returned when a `Transport`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html)
- A sink that delivers OpenLineage events to a backend.

---

# CloudClientTransport in datafusion_openlineage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/struct.CloudClientTransport.html

`pub struct CloudClientTransport { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Posts OpenLineage events to an HTTP endpoint via [ CloudClient](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html).

Single events go to `endpoint`; batches go to `batch_endpoint` (by default the
single endpoint with `/batch` appended, matching the OpenLineage HTTP API).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/cloud.rs.html#49)#### pub fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)(client: [CloudClient](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html), endpoint: [Url](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/url/struct.Url.html)) -> [CloudClientTransport](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudClientTransport.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/cloud.rs.html#49)

#### pub fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)(client: [CloudClient](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html), endpoint: [Url](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/url/struct.Url.html)) -> [CloudClientTransport](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudClientTransport.html)

Use a pre-built [ CloudClient](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html) (e.g. one constructed with cloud
credentials via

[/](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html#method.new_aws)

`CloudClient::new_aws`[).](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html#method.new_databricks)

`CloudClient::new_databricks`The batch endpoint defaults to `endpoint` with `/batch` appended; the
request timeout defaults to [ DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/config/constant.DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.html). Override either
with

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudClientTransport.html#method.with_batch_endpoint)

`Self::with_batch_endpoint`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudClientTransport.html#method.with_timeout)

`Self::with_timeout`[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/cloud.rs.html#60)#### pub fn [with_token](https://docs.rs#method.with_token)(endpoint: [Url](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/url/struct.Url.html), token: impl [ToString](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html)) -> [CloudClientTransport](https://docs.rs/struct.CloudClientTransport.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/cloud.rs.html#60)

A dataset consumed or produced by a run.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.namespace)

`namespace: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Namespace the dataset belongs to.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.name)

`name: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Dataset name, unique within its namespace.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.facets)

`facets: `[DatasetFacets](https://docs.rs/facets/struct.DatasetFacets.html)Dataset-level facets carrying additional metadata.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.input_facets)

`input_facets: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[InputDatasetFacets](https://docs.rs/facets/struct.InputDatasetFacets.html)>Input-only facets (e.g. runtime statistics). Serialized as `inputFacets`
and only present on input datasets.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.output_facets)

`output_facets: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[OutputDatasetFacets](https://docs.rs/facets/struct.OutputDatasetFacets.html)>Output-only facets (e.g. runtime statistics). Serialized as
`outputFacets` and only present on output datasets.

# DatasetName in datafusion_openlineage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage/0.0.7/datafusion_openlineage/struct.DatasetName.html

## Expand description

An OpenLineage dataset name: a `namespace` plus a `name` unique within it.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.namespace)

`namespace: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The dataset’s namespace (e.g. a storage root or job namespace).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.name)

`name: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The dataset’s name, unique within its namespace.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/naming.rs.html#17)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-DatasetName)### impl [DatasetName](https://docs.rs/struct.DatasetName.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/naming.rs.html#24)#### pub fn [from_location](https://docs.rs#method.from_location)(url: &[Url](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/url/struct.Url.html)) -> [DatasetName](https://docs.rs/struct.DatasetName.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/naming.rs.html#24)

#### pub fn [from_location](https://docs.rs#method.from_location)(url: &[Url](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/url/struct.Url.html)) -> [DatasetName](https://docs.rs/struct.DatasetName.html)

Map a storage location URL to its OpenLineage `(namespace, name)`.

- `s3://bucket/key...`-> namespace- `s3://bucket`, name- `key...`
- `gs://bucket/key...`-> namespace- `gs://bucket`, name- `key...`
- `file:///path`-> namespace- `file`, name- `/path`
- anything else        -> namespace `{scheme}://{host}`, name`{path}`

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/naming.rs.html#52)#### pub fn [from_table_ref](https://docs.rs#method.from_table_ref)(default_namespace: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), table_ref: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [DatasetName](https://docs.rs/struct.DatasetName.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/naming.rs.html#52)

#### pub fn [from_table_ref](https://docs.rs#method.from_table_ref)(default_namespace: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), table_ref: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [DatasetName](https://docs.rs/struct.DatasetName.html)

A fallback name for a table reference that has no resolvable location (e.g. an in-memory or unqualified table). Uses the configured job namespace so it still lands somewhere sensible.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/context.rs.html#47)#### pub fn [from_env](https://docs.rs#method.from_env)(config: &[OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)) -> [LineageContext](https://docs.rs/struct.LineageContext.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/openlineage_client/context.rs.html#47)

#### pub fn [from_env](https://docs.rs#method.from_env)(config: &[OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)) -> [LineageContext](https://docs.rs/struct.LineageContext.html)

Build a context from the established OpenLineage parent-run environment
conventions, returning `None`-filled fields when nothing is set.

Reads `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_ID` (slash form `{namespace}/{name}/{runId}`),
falling back to the discrete `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_JOB_NAMESPACE` /
`OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_JOB_NAME` / `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_RUN_ID` variables.

[§](https://docs.rs#method.flush)

Flushes any internally-buffered events, blocking until they are delivered
(or fail). Called by

[after the drain queue empties. The default is a no-op — override it only for transports that buffer beyond a single](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.shutdown)`OpenLineageClient::shutdown`[call.](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#tymethod.emit)`emit`[Read more](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#method.flush)## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

### Config([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))

The client could not be built from the given configuration or environment — for example, no Tokio runtime was available to host the drain task, or an endpoint URL was malformed.
